current_flow: warehouse-schema builds the fresh WAREHOUSE ingest/DDL layer on the separate WAREHOUSE_PG_* Postgres: a write pool + ingestion repository distinct from the read-only query port, a committed Drizzle migration applied by warehouse:migrate, the ingest_batch registry (≤1 active per source_kind+period, atomic flip), sap_transaction (raw lines, numeric(18,2), UNIQUE source-line identity, indexed), mis_budget, and the actual_by_key_month gold view. snake_case per decision 0015. No loader/API, no read-port change, no semantic registration.
new_abstractions: the warehouse write pool + ingestion repository (separate from the read-only port)
the ingest_batch registry with a ≤1-active partial unique index + atomic flip
sap_transaction (numeric paise, UNIQUE source-line identity) + mis_budget
the actual_by_key_month gold view with named columns

criteria_map.a reproducible warehouse:migrate creates: KEEP. Reproducible warehouse:migrate APPLIES committed SQL (generate-once) via a SEPARATE write pool/ingestion repository; the read-only query port is out of write_scope and untouched (findings 1,2,3).
criteria_map.ingest_batch enforces at most one active: KEEP (amended). At-most-one active per (source_kind, period) via a partial unique index + an atomic candidate-load-then-flip; source_kind CHECK; UNIQUE(batch_id,txn_no,line_id) blocks double-count; numeric(18,2) paise; FK+key indexes (findings 6,7,8,10).
criteria_map.actual_by_key_month is a plain view over: KEEP. actual_by_key_month is a plain view over the ACTIVE batch with named columns (plant,cost_center,gl_code,month,actual_net); proven by a fixed seed fixture (finding 5,8).

gaps: The declared scope cannot create the Drizzle warehouse config: drizzle.config.ts targets only the app schema and no separate warehouse config file was in scope
write_scope (backend/src/warehouse/) authorized editing the read-only postgres.adapter.ts / warehouse.interface.ts, contradicting the acceptance criterion and reviewer focus
warehouse:migrate coupled generation to application (drizzle-kit generate each run), which mutates artifacts and is not a reproducible apply
verify_commands omitted npm run test:hermetic (and verify.py), so the changed quality-gate guard / test:hermetic wiring could break while the task closes green
The live-proof procedure ('insert two seeded rows') gave no batch values, keys, amounts, expected result, or rerun behaviour, and the hermetic test could pass while the committed view SQL fails
The active-batch invariant was underspecified: 'exactly one' vs a partial unique index's 'at most one', no source_kind check, month encoding, or atomic load/switch/concurrency protocol
The batch grain conflicted with the full-July requirement: a 31-plant file vs per-(plant) active state, with no stated whole-file-vs-per-plant batch or atomic full-file replace
Table contracts were insufficient: mis_budget had no grain; sap_transaction omitted ContraAct and a source-line unique identity (duplicate rows double the gold); the view had no named output columns
The schema designed against the database constitution (snake_case/uploaded_at vs PascalCase/camelCase/AtUtc) without a recorded fresh-code deviation (decision 0013)
Warehouse auditability was guessed: uploaded_by cannot FK across separate Postgres instances, and there was no fail-fast guard against unset/misdirected WAREHOUSE_PG_*
Active-decision reconciliation was stale: the approved story plan's decisions_reviewed ends at 0013 while 0014 (and now 0015) govern this task
resolutions: Added backend/drizzle-warehouse.config.ts (+ backend/drizzle-warehouse/) to write_scope for a separate warehouse Drizzle config.
Narrowed write_scope to the specific NEW files; the read-only postgres.adapter.ts / warehouse.interface.ts are excluded and must stay unchanged.
The migration SQL is generated ONCE and committed; warehouse:migrate only APPLIES the committed folder via the warehouse pool (a ts-node runner mirroring db/migrate.ts).
verify_commands now include npm run test:hermetic so stage-done exercises the guard + test wiring.

Replaced with an exact deterministic seed fixture (a named script inserting specified rows into one active batch with an expected actual_net) run as demonstrated host evidence; the hermetic test asserts the schema module shape only.
Specified: a partial unique index giving AT MOST ONE active per (source_kind, period), a source_kind CHECK, month as a first-of-month date, and an atomic candidate-load-then-flip in one transaction.

Batch grain = one whole-file batch per (source_kind, period) (canonical_plant is a row attribute), per the client's full-July-batch decision (Q1); a re-upload atomically flips the active pointer for the period.

sap_transaction gains contra_account + UNIQUE(batch_id, txn_no, line_id) (no double-count); mis_budget grain defined (format_id, period, line_id, gl_code, cost_center, budget/rollover amounts); actual_by_key_month exposes named columns (plant, cost_center, gl_code, month, actual_net).
Recorded decision 0015-warehouse-snake-case-deviation (accepted): the warehouse uses snake_case + *_utc as a warehouse-scoped deviation; audit columns, FK indexes, and numeric(18,2) still apply.
uploaded_by is a TEXT app-user id (no cross-DB FK); the write pool fails fast if WAREHOUSE_PG_* is unset/misdirected so tables are never created in the wrong DB.
Decisions 0014 and 0015 are attested in this task's plan/contract; the approved story-plan header predates them (0014/0015 were created during planning) and is reconciled at the task level.

rounds.question: The warehouse schema is fresh backend code. The app constitution (pnp-database-standards, decision 0013) requires PascalCase tables / camelCase columns / AtUtc timestamps, but the architecture doc and standard analytics/warehouse convention use snake_case (sap_transaction, cost_center, actual_by_key_month). Which naming for the WAREHOUSE schema?

summary: One cold read returned eleven findings. Ten are repository-answerable and resolved in the amended contract + plan (drizzle-warehouse config, narrowed scope off the read-only port, generate-once/apply-only migrate, test:hermetic in verify_commands, a deterministic seed fixture, the ≤1-active partial-unique + atomic flip, whole-file batch grain per the client's Q1, contra_account + UNIQUE source-line identity + mis_budget grain + named view columns, uploaded_by as a TEXT id + a fail-fast WAREHOUSE_PG_* guard, and the 0014/0015 attestation). The one genuine decision — the warehouse naming convention — went to the human, who chose snake_case, now recorded as accepted decision 0015. Verdict pass.
